subject: BYM model with more rows than polygons

messages.author: 419a40da673a6664
messages.subject: BYM model with more rows than polygons
parts:
Hello,
I have data from a poll conducted in a sample from public hospitals across the country, in which people were asked whether they had a certain disease and different covariates such as weight, age, sex, etc. The number of people polled in each hospital is not constant, and I'm trying to fit a BYM model using the data from each individual without summarizing it per polygon. This means that I have more rows in the data frame than polygons, with a column named ID that indicates where does each row belong to.

I tried using the following formula:
 count ~ 1 + covariate_1 + sex + age_category + f(ID, model = "bym", graph = vecinos, scale.model = TRUE),

where the graph was obtained using sp::poly2nb.

I'm not sure if I've got the internal mechanics right. I don't know how INLA matches the graph with the data frame. My guess is that it uses the covariate you want to apply the Besag-York-Mollié model to, so that in this case, since ID has the same number of unique values as the number of nodes in the graph, it simply matches the first value to the first node, which in turn would mean that the model produces similar fitted values within each polygon (which was actually the case when I tried it), and I can just average the results per aerial unit, and then just join the results to the original spatial polygons data frame, but I don't have any certainty that that's what INLA is doing.

What's the correct way to specify the model?

Thank you,
Bernardo
